newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker despite rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker despite rate cut.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in thin trading on Monday, following a long rallying phase in Canadian fixed income markets.
"Corrective action from a couple months worth of rises," said Technical Data market analyst Jeoff Hall.

Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.90 to C$108.80 to yield 7.248 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 8/32 to yield 6.84 percent, so the spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 41 basis points from 37 points at Friday's close.
Today the Bank of Canada cut its key bank rate by 25 basis points to 3.50 percent. The move lowered the bank's target range for the overnight lending rate to 3.0-3.5 percent from 3.25-3.75 percent.
The bank rate, which has changed in nature over the past decades, is now at its lowest level since August 1963.
The drop in interest rates was "largely anticipated," said senior economist Mark Chandler at Goldman Sachs Canada.
"We've had three rate cuts in the course of a month, which...is pretty aggressive," Chandler said. Canada's central bank has chopped short-term rates 10 times so far this year.

Both agreed that Canadian bonds have rallied strongly over the last while. "We've been going at a pretty tremendous speed there," Hall said. Spreads between Canadian and U.S. bonds have narrowed dramatically in the past few weeks.

In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.60 to C$102.48 to yield 6.657 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 5/32 to yield 6.56 percent. The spread widened to 10 basis points from three at Friday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.19 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.16 percent.
